#284([PRD] Repair Frontend Deep Module — extract repair/ + split god page (3 PRs))

## What to build

Create the new deep module folder `client/src/features/repairs/repair/` with a public barrel (`index.ts`) and four sub-files: `types.ts`, `adapters.ts`, `formatters.ts`, `domain.ts`. The sub-files are skeletal — they re-export existing content and add nothing new yet (that comes in later slices). `client/src/features/repairs/api.ts` becomes a thin re-export from `repair/adapters.ts`. Zero behavior change.

This is the **foundation slice** for the rest of the PRD. The public surface of the barrel is the new contract every other slice builds on, so it warrants a quick `architect` skill pass before subsequent slices land.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `client/src/features/repairs/repair/` folder exists with `index.ts`, `types.ts`, `adapters.ts`, `formatters.ts`, `domain.ts`.
- [ ] `repair/index.ts` exports a minimal public surface (at minimum: `RepairStatus` and the empty adapter/formatter/domain sub-modules).
- [ ] `repair/types.ts` re-exports the canonical types from `shared/types/repair.ts` (`RepairStatus`, `Repair`, `RepairDetail`, `RepairLineItem`, `WorkLog`, `RepairIntakeInput`, `LaborService`, `HoldReason`, `VALID_TRANSITIONS`).
- [ ] `repair/adapters.ts`, `repair/formatters.ts`, `repair/domain.ts` exist as files but are empty / placeholder content (to be filled by later slices).
- [ ] `client/src/features/repairs/api.ts` is reduced to thin re-exports of whatever adapters exist (or remains a re-export of the existing internal functions until later slices migrate them).
- [ ] No file outside the new `repair/` folder is modified except `api.ts`.
- [ ] All existing tests pass without modification.
- [ ] No new `as` type assertions in production code.
- [ ] `architect` skill has been invoked and signed off on the barrel's public surface (HITL for this slice only).

## Parent PRD (#284)

## Source

- Handoff: [`.tmp/handoff-repair-frontend-deep-module.md`](../../.tmp/handoff-repair-frontend-deep-module.md)
- Origin: `improve-codebase-architecture` analysis of `client/src/features/repairs/` (2026-06-05)
- Architecture already agreed with the user — this PRD packages it for implementation.

## Problem Statement

The `client/src/features/repairs/` feature has **5,158 lines across 9 components** and **no deep module** behind them. The backend (`server/src/services/repair.service.ts`) is genuinely deep — it owns the atomic complete-repair transaction, the status state machine, hold-reason validation, and the cross-entity orchestration, applied per [ADR-008 (Flow-First Architecture)](../../docs/40-decisions/ADR-008-flow-first-architecture.md). The client side never received the same treatment.

The symptoms are concrete and visible:

- **Types re-declared 3 times.** The enriched `RepairDetail` shape lives in `shared/types/repair.ts` (canonical), `api.ts` (re-declared as `RepairDetailResponse`), and `RepairDetailPage.tsx` (re-declared again as a 60-line structural copy). Three places to keep in sync; the canonical version is imported by zero components.
- **Format helpers re-implemented 3+ times.** `formatStatus` appears in `RepairCard.tsx`, `RepairListPage.tsx`, and `RepairRowExpandPanel.tsx` with identical bodies. `epochToInputDate` / `inputDateToEpoch` is in two files. `getWorkerName` is in three. The deletion test fails for each of them.
- **The same `fetch('/api/users')` call lives in three components** (list page, calendar view, detail page). If the workers endpoint ever changes shape, three call sites break.
- **`RepairDetailPage.tsx` is 2,078 lines with 20+ `useState` and 7 `useEffect`.** It bundles 7+ orthogonal concerns (timer, customer notes, internal notes, planned date, pickup date, line items, worker assignment, status transition, payment, special items) in one component. Every test of any one concern has to render the entire page.
- **A real bug has shipped.** The four KPI cards on the list page ("Active / In progress / Ready for pickup / Overdue") iterate over the **current page's** `repairs` array, not the full dataset. "Active: 7" actually means "active on this page". No test catches this because no test exercises the KPI block — the fact that the bug shipped is itself a symptom of the shallow architecture.

The combination is the classic shallow-module pattern: a deep backend service behind a thin fan of duplicated, page-scoped client adapters. ADR-008 was accepted but only applied to one side.

## Solution

Add a deep frontend module — `client/src/features/repairs/repair/` — that owns the **enriched repair shape, the fetch adapters, the formatters, the status-machine and VAT-rate domain constants, and a per-entity hook facade** (`useRepairList`, `useRepairDetail`, `useRepairCalendar`). Above that, add three **focused interaction hooks** (`useRepairTimer`, `useRepairNotes`, `useRepairLineItems`) for the high-leverage concerns on the detail page. Extract three **section components** (`TimerSection`, `NotesSection`, `LineItemsSection`) and the previously-inline `SpecialItemForm`. The detail page becomes a pure orchestrator that composes hooks and renders sections.

The detail cache is shared across the list page's inline row expand and the full detail page via a module-level `Map<id, { data, fetchedAt }>` in `useRepairDetail` — when one warms the cache, the other hits warm. No global store, no React context.

The KPI bug is fixed structurally: `useRepairList` returns a `breakdown: Record<RepairStatus, number>` field that the server computes alongside the paginated rows. The KPI block renders from the breakdown, not from iterating rows. The bug becomes impossible to reintroduce because the totals are the hook's job, not the page's.

The work is delivered as **three independently-shippable PRs**, each with its own review surface:

- **PR 1** — deep module + per-entity data hooks + KPI fix (no user-visible change beyond correct KPI totals).
- **PR 2** — `useRepairTimer` + `TimerSection`, `useRepairNotes` + `NotesSection` (no user-visible change; page shrinks to ~1,400 lines).
- **PR 3** — `useRepairLineItems` + `LineItemsSection` + `SpecialItemForm` extraction (no user-visible change; page lands at ~250 lines).

## User Stories

### Data layer

1. As a frontend developer, I want a single deep module to import the repair types from, so that I never re-declare a `RepairDetail` shape, an enriched-line-items type, or a status constant.
2. As a frontend developer, I want one place to change a field name in the enriched repair shape, so that I do not chase 3 re-declared copies through 9 files.
3. As a frontend developer, I want a `fetchWorkers()` adapter in the deep module, so that the three components that today call `fetch('/api/users')` inline converge on a single shape and a single URL.
4. As a frontend developer, I want a `searchParts(query)` adapter, so that the parts search in the detail page is not its own one-off inline `fetch`.
5. As a frontend developer, I want a `fetchLaborServices()` adapter, so that the labor tab does not embed its own URL.
6. As a frontend developer, I want format helpers (`formatStatus`, `formatDate`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDuration`, `epochToInputDate`, `inputDateToEpoch`) in one tested file, so that I can fix a date-formatting bug in one place.
7. As a frontend developer, I want `VALID_TRANSITIONS`, `ACTIVE_STATUSES`, and the VAT-rate-ID mapping in a single domain file, so that the status machine and the "what is a valid VAT rate" knowledge live next to each other.
8. As a frontend developer, I want the date-anchor logic (plannedDate with createdAt fallback) in the deep module, so that the calendar view, the reschedule popover, and any future surface converge on the same answer to "what date anchors this repair?".

### Per-entity hooks

9. As a frontend developer, I want a `useRepairList({ filters, page })` hook, so that the list page does not own its own fetch state, error state, or pagination state.
10. As a frontend developer, I want `useRepairList` to return `breakdown: Record<RepairStatus, number>`, so that the KPI block shows accurate counts without iterating the page's rows.
11. As a frontend developer, I want a `useRepairDetail(id)` hook with a module-level cache, so that when the list page's row expand warms the cache, the detail page's mount hits warm — no double-fetch when a user expands a row and then opens the full detail page.
12. As a frontend developer, I want `useRepairDetail` mutations to invalidate the cache entry, so that local state stays in sync with the server after a status transition, a note edit, or a line item change.
13. As a frontend developer, I want a `useRepairCalendar({ initialDate })` hook, so that the calendar view does not own its own week-boundary math, refetch triggers, or active-status filter.
14. As a frontend developer, I want the per-entity hooks to expose `{ data, loading, error, refetch }` in a uniform shape, so that the page can wire any of them into a loading-spinner / error-banner / retry pattern without per-hook branching.

### Focused interaction hooks (detail page extraction)

15. As a frontend developer, I want a `useRepairTimer(repairId)` hook, so that timer start/stop/tick state lives in one tested place and the detail page is not a 2,000-line timer implementation.
16. As a frontend developer, I want the "no assigned worker" rule enforced by `useRepairTimer`, so that the page does not need to remember it.
17. As a frontend developer, I want a `useRepairNotes(repair, { kind: 'customer' | 'internal' })` hook, so that the two parallel notes state machines (customer and internal) are not duplicated in the page.
18. As a frontend developer, I want a `useRepairLineItems(repairId)` hook, so that line item add/edit/delete + the special-item workflow live in one tested place and the detail page is not a 2,000-line line-item table.
19. As a frontend developer, I want `useRepairLineItems` to own the two-step special-item workflow (create part → add as line item) as a single function call, so that the orchestration is not inline JSX in a sub-component of a sub-component.
20. As a future developer, I want any of the three focused interaction hooks to be reusable from the calendar view (e.g. "timer running" indicator on a card), so that I do not have to re-implement the same state machine.

### Section components

21. As a frontend developer, I want a `TimerSection.tsx` file, so that the timer section is a small, testable, presentational component that takes a hook return value and renders UI.
22. As a frontend developer, I want a `NotesSection.tsx` file that takes `kind` and renders either the customer or internal notes UI, so that the two notes blocks do not duplicate their state-machine code.
23. As a frontend developer, I want a `LineItemsSection.tsx` file that owns the parts search, labor services dropdown, line item table, and totals, so that all of that lives in one file.
24. As a frontend developer, I want `SpecialItemForm.tsx` as a top-level component file, so that the workflow is not trapped inside `RepairDetailPage.tsx` and could be reused in `RepairIntakeModal` or the POS cart in the future.
25. As a frontend developer, I want the `RepairDetailPage` to be a thin orchestrator that wires the deep module's hooks and the focused interaction hooks to the section components, so that the page file shrinks to ~250 lines and is a readable, reviewable, navigable page.

### Bug fix

26. As a manager looking at the KPI block, I want "Active: 23 / In progress: 12 / Ready: 4" to reflect the **full filtered set**, not the current page's rows, so that the numbers are accurate and trustworthy.
27. As a future developer, I want the KPI bug to be structurally impossible to reintroduce, so that no future refactor of the list page silently re-introduces page-scoped iteration.

### Test surface

28. As a frontend developer, I want pure-function tests for `repair/formatters.ts` and `repair/domain.ts`, so that I can fix a date-formatting or status-machine bug with a fast unit test.
29. As a frontend developer, I want focused hook tests for each of the new focused interaction hooks, so that a bug in the timer state machine is exercised in isolation — not via rendering the entire detail page.
30. As a frontend developer, I want the existing tests for unaffected components (`RepairCard`, `RepairIntakeModal`, `RepairRowExpandPanel`, `ReschedulePopover`, `RepairCalendarView`) to keep passing without modification, so that this PRD is provably behaviour-preserving for the surfaces that did not change.

## Implementation Decisions

### Deep module shape (F.1)

A new folder `client/src/features/repairs/repair/` with the following files:

- `index.ts` — barrel, the public face. Anything not exported here is module-internal.
- `types.ts` — re-exports from `shared/types/repair.ts`; adds client-side shapes (e.g. `PaginatedRepairs`, the `breakdown` field).
- `adapters.ts` — fetch wrappers: `createRepair`, `getRepair`, `transitionRepairStatus`, `updateRepairNotes`, `getCustomerWithBicycles`, `startWorkTimer`, `stopWorkTimer`, `getRepairs`, `completeRepairPayment`, `getRepairsForWeek`, plus the new `fetchWorkers()`, `searchParts()`, `fetchLaborServices()`. URL builders centralised here.
- `formatters.ts` — pure functions: `formatStatus`, `formatDate`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDuration`, `formatElapsed`, `epochToInputDate`, `inputDateToEpoch`, `getDateAnchor` (moved from `utils/dateAnchor.ts` and re-exported there for backward compatibility).
- `domain.ts` — `VALID_TRANSITIONS` (re-exported from `shared/types/repair.ts`), `ACTIVE_STATUSES`, `TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `isActiveStatus`, `isTerminalStatus`, `VAT_RATE_IDS`, `vatRateIdForBps`, `getWorkerName` (if it stays as a one-liner in components, this is optional).

### Per-entity hooks

Three hooks, each a thin coordinator over an adapter plus state:

- `useRepairList({ filters, page })` → `{ repairs, total, totalPages, breakdown, loading, error, refetch }`. Internally uses `getRepairs`.
- `useRepairDetail(id)` → `{ data: RepairDetail | null, loading, error, refresh, update }`. Internally uses a module-level `Map<id, { data, fetchedAt }>` shared across all callers. On a fresh call, returns the cached value if any; on a mutation, invalidates the entry. The `update` method is a generic patch that re-fetches after success.
- `useRepairCalendar({ initialDate })` → `{ repairs, weekStart, weekEnd, isLoading, error, goPrev, goNext, goToday, refetch }`. Internally uses `getRepairsForWeek` and the `mondayOf()` helper (currently inside `useRepairsForWeek.ts`).

The cache strategy for `useRepairDetail` is **module-level `Map<id, { data, fetchedAt }>`** with no TTL (matches current behavior of `useRepairDetailCache`). Mutations call `invalidate(id)` before re-fetching. No global store, no React context, no external dependency.

### Focused interaction hooks

Three hooks in `client/src/features/repairs/hooks/`:

- `useRepairTimer(repairId)` → `{ activeTimer, elapsedMs, isRunning, canStart, error, start, stop }`. Owns the timer state machine: start calls `startWorkTimer`, sets up a tick interval, exposes `elapsedMs`; stop calls `stopWorkTimer`, clears the interval, invalidates the `useRepairDetail` cache. The "needs an assigned worker" rule is enforced inside the hook (`canStart: false` when no worker is assigned).
- `useRepairNotes(repair, { kind: 'customer' | 'internal' })` → `{ isEditing, tempValue, isSaving, error, startEdit, cancelEdit, save, change }`. Single hook covers both notes kinds by parameterising the field it reads/writes. The save cycle calls `updateRepairNotes` and updates local state.
- `useRepairLineItems(repairId)` → `{ add(part | labor | special), update(itemId, qty, price), remove(itemId) }`. Owns the special-item workflow as `add({ kind: 'special', name, priceCents, vatRateBps, quantity })` — internally does the two-step `POST /api/parts/special` → `POST /repairs/:id/items` and returns the new line item. Refreshes the `useRepairDetail` cache on every successful operation.

### Section components

Three new files in `client/src/features/repairs/components/`:

- `TimerSection.tsx` — pure presentational, consumes `useRepairTimer`.
- `NotesSection.tsx` — pure presentational, takes `kind: 'customer' | 'internal'` and consumes `useRepairNotes`.
- `LineItemsSection.tsx` — pure presentational, consumes `useRepairLineItems`. Includes the parts search (consumes `searchParts`), the labor services dropdown (consumes `fetchLaborServices`), the line item table, and the totals panel.
- `SpecialItemForm.tsx` — extracted from the inline 120-line sub-component inside `RepairDetailPage.tsx`. Calls into `useRepairLineItems().add({ kind: 'special', ... })` instead of doing the orchestration itself.

### KPI bug fix — server change

Extend the existing `GET /api/repairs` paginated response with a new field:

```
{
  repairs: [...],
  total: 23,
  page: 1,
  pageSize: 20,
  totalPages: 2,
  breakdown: { intake: 1, in_progress: 12, on_hold: 2, verified: 3, ready: 4, completed: 0, cancelled: 1 }
}
```

Server computes the breakdown in the same query (or in a follow-up cheap query) for the active filter set (excluding pagination). Client reads it via `useRepairList` and renders the KPI block from it. The bug becomes structurally impossible because the page no longer iterates rows to compute totals.

This is a **tiny** server change: one new field on the response, one line in the list query, one line in the route. Shared types updated in `shared/types/repair.ts` (`PaginatedRepairs` interface gains `breakdown`).

### Migration order (3 PRs, one PRD)

- **PR 1** — `repair/` folder created; `api.ts` becomes a thin re-export; per-entity hooks added; existing components migrate to the new module; `useRepairDetailCache` and `useRepairsForWeek` deleted; KPI bug fix lands (server + client).
- **PR 2** — `useRepairTimer` + `TimerSection`; `useRepairNotes` + `NotesSection`; corresponding section blocks in `RepairDetailPage` reduced to one-line components.
- **PR 3** — `useRepairLineItems` + `LineItemsSection`; `SpecialItemForm` extracted; corresponding section block in `RepairDetailPage` reduced to one-line component; `RepairDetailPage` lands at ~250 lines.

Each PR keeps `RepairDetailPage` working throughout — the page is reduced incrementally, not rewritten in one shot.

### Public surface preservation

`api.ts` becomes a thin re-export from `repair/adapters.ts`. The existing imports `import { createRepair } from '../api.js'` resolve unchanged during PR 1's migration, then the import sites are updated to point at `repair` directly in a follow-up cleanup (or in the same PR, depending on churn size). No test file needs to update its imports of `api.ts` for behaviour to be preserved.

`utils/dateAnchor.ts` stays at its current path and re-exports `getDateAnchor` from `repair/formatters.ts`, so existing imports keep working. The function's canonical home is `repair/formatters.ts`.

### Naming

- `useRepairList`, `useRepairDetail`, `useRepairCalendar` — match the backend resource names.
- `useRepairTimer`, `useRepairNotes`, `useRepairLineItems` — match the concern names already used in component-level comments.
- `TimerSection`, `NotesSection`, `LineItemsSection` — match the section titles already rendered in the page.
- `SpecialItemForm` — extracted name matches its current inline sub-component.

### Constraints respected

- **No `as` type assertions** in production code (CONTEXT.md). The shallow-modules-being-merged don't currently use `as`; the merge must not introduce any.
- **Features own their types** (CONTEXT.md). The deep module re-exports shared types but does not move them out of `shared/`. The `breakdown` field is added to the existing `PaginatedRepairs` interface in `shared/types/repair.ts`.
- **Flow-first naming** (ADR-008). The deep module is named `repair/`, not `repair-client` or `repair.service.ts`.
- **`data-testid` is project-wide convention** (ADR-010). New section components expose `data-testid` attributes; the E2E test for the repairs flow (future, per ADR-010 scope expansion) consumes them.
- **No `as` in production code** (CONTEXT.md). Same as above.
- **No new dependencies** (no React Query, no SWR, no date-fns, no zod on the client). The module-level `Map` is the cache; pure TypeScript handles everything else.

## Testing Decisions

### What makes a good test here

A good test exercises the **public interface of the deep module** (the barrel exports) and the **public interface of each hook** (its return value shape). It does not assert on internal helper call order, and it does not duplicate existing component tests — it complements them.

### Per-layer test plan

| Layer | Test file | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `repair/formatters.ts` | `repair/__tests__/formatters.test.ts` | All pure format functions, edge cases (null, epoch=0, leap years) |
| `repair/domain.ts` | `repair/__tests__/domain.test.ts` | Status machine, VAT mapping, date anchor |
| `repair/adapters.ts` | `repair/__tests__/adapters.test.ts` | URL building, query string shape, error mapping (replaces/evolves `__tests__/api.test.ts`) |
| `useRepairList` | `hooks/__tests__/useRepairList.test.ts` | Filter changes reset page, breakdown field is returned, error retry, refetch |
| `useRepairDetail` | `hooks/__tests__/useRepairDetail.test.ts` (evolved from `useRepairDetailCache.test.ts`) | Cache hit/miss, mutation invalidation, error state |
| `useRepairCalendar` | `hooks/__tests__/useRepairCalendar.test.ts` (evolved from `useRepairsForWeek.test.ts`) | Week boundaries, navigation, refetch trigger |
| `useRepairTimer` | `hooks/__tests__/useRepairTimer.test.ts` | Start/stop cycle, tick correctness, canStart guard, error states |
| `useRepairNotes` | `hooks/__tests__/useRepairNotes.test.ts` | Edit/save cycle, kind parameter, validation, error states |
| `useRepairLineItems` | `hooks/__tests__/useRepairLineItems.test.ts` | Add part, add labor, add special (two-step), update, remove |
| `TimerSection`, `NotesSection`, `LineItemsSection`, `SpecialItemForm` | `components/__tests__/*` | Render states, user interactions, hook contract enforcement |

### What is NOT deleted (yet)

- `useRepairDetailCache.test.ts` is **renamed** to `useRepairDetail.test.ts` and extended. It is not deleted.
- `useRepairsForWeek.test.ts` is **renamed** to `useRepairCalendar.test.ts` and extended. It is not deleted.
- `__tests__/api.test.ts` is **replaced** by `repair/__tests__/adapters.test.ts`. The old file is deleted in the same PR that adds the new one.

### What survives unchanged

- `components/__tests__/RepairCard.test.tsx` — does not touch the god page.
- `components/__tests__/RepairIntakeModal.test.tsx` — does not touch the god page.
- `components/__tests__/RepairRowExpandPanel.test.tsx` — does not touch the god page; only its import of `RepairDetailResponse` is updated to import from the new deep module.
- `components/__tests__/ReschedulePopover.test.tsx` — does not touch the god page.
- `components/__tests__/RepairCalendarView.test.tsx` — does not touch the god page.

## Out of Scope

These are explicitly out of scope for this PRD — separate handoffs are needed for each:

- `useRepairDates`, `useRepairWorkerAssignment`, `useRepairStatusTransition` — the remaining 4 focused interaction hooks. Same pattern as the 3 in-scope hooks; smaller scope per hook. Estimated: 1 follow-up PRD.
- The custom combobox extraction (`useCombobox` + `<Combobox>` in `client/src/shared/ui/`) — natural follow-up after this PRD lands; ~4 callsites in the repairs feature would benefit (parts search, labor dropdown, bicycle dropdown in intake, worker combobox in `FilterBar`). Estimated: 1 follow-up PRD.
- Adopting TanStack Query / SWR — a separate ADR. The module-level `Map` is the right size for now.
- The `useRepairList` breakdown **history over time** (i.e. "KPI block should also show yesterday's count"). Currently a single-snapshot KPI; trend data is a separate concern.
- The `RepairsPage` route refactor — the page remains a route entry; the deep module + hooks is the new structure behind it. No route-level changes.
- E2E tests for the repairs flow. ADR-010 scope expansion is a separate ADR; the E2E conventions are respected (`data-testid` on new section components) so a future E2E PRD can land without rework.
- The labor-catalog extraction as its own bounded context (`labor-catalog/`).
- Status history / audit trail surfacing in the UI. `shared/types/repair.ts` has the `RepairStatusHistory` type; no client code uses it. Surfacing it is a separate concern.
- Other candidates from the `improve-codebase-architecture` analysis: candidates 3 (KPI bug — **in scope, fixed in PR 1**), 4 (`SpecialItemForm` — **in scope, extracted in PR 3**), 5 (combobox — **out of scope, follow-up**).

## Open Questions (Surfaced for the Builder)

1. **Where does the `breakdown` get computed on the server?** Single query (e.g. `SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM repairs WHERE ... GROUP BY status`) or two queries (rows + counts)? **Default: two queries in the same handler** — keeps the row query untouched and is cheap enough at the expected scale. Decide during PR 1.

# Pi Pos V1 — Context

## Domain Overview

Pi POS is a reusable starter platform for AI-assisted projects using controlled, step-by-step engineering. It implements a point-of-sale system split across three packages: frontend client, backend server, and shared types/validations.

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| **Frontend** | React 18 + TypeScript 5 + Vite + Tailwind CSS 3 + Radix UI + Zustand + React Router 6.x (v7 data API) + react-hot-toast |
| **Backend** | Hono 4 + Drizzle ORM + better-sqlite3 |
| **Validation** | Zod (shared between frontend and backend) |
| **Testing** | Vitest (unit, integration) + Playwright (E2E — see [ADR-010](docs/40-decisions/ADR-010-e2e-test-strategy.md)) |
| **Package Manager** | pnpm |

## Architecture

```
client/          # React frontend app
server/          # Node.js API server
shared/          # Types and Zod schemas used by both
```

### Key Principles

1. **Flow-first architecture (target)** — Core transaction logic lives in deep modules (`sale.service.ts`) rather than scattered across feature folders. Features own their UI and routes; services own the business orchestration.
2. **Event-driven communication** — Components fire domain events via `appEvents.emit()`; the app shell maps events to side effects (notifications, store updates).
3. **Flat global state** — Only cross-cutting concerns live in global Zustand stores (sidebar, theme). Features keep their own stores scoped to themselves.
4. **Clean layer boundaries** — Request flow: Routes → Services → Repositories. Mutations use `useFetcher` on the frontend.
5. **Explicit theming** — CSS variables defined in a single file (`client/src/index.css`). Change once, update everywhere.

### Frontend (`client/`)

## Key Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| **Customer** | Shop customer — private individual or company. Private customers require `firstName` + `lastName`; companies require `companyName`. Address fields: `street`, `number`, `bus`, `postalCode`, `city`, `country` (default `'BE'`). Optional `email`, `phone`, `vatId`, `notificationPreference`. Can be unattached to a sale (walk-in). |
| **Direct Sale** | The core POS transaction: customer selects parts from stock, pays via single method, sale is created atomically with stock deduction. `sourceType='direct_sale'`. |
| **Part / Product** | Sellable inventory item stored in the `parts` table. Domain term is "part"; code sometimes uses "product" interchangeably. Has name, optional SKU/barcode, price, and denormalized stock count. |
| **Sale Cart** | Client-side Zustand store holding part line items (partId, quantity, unitPriceNet, vatRateId) awaiting checkout. Lives entirely in the browser until submitted. |
| **Walk-in Sale** | A sale with no customer attached (`sales.customerId` is NULL). Anonymous transaction. |
| **Stock Movement** | Immutable audit row recording every inventory change. `quantityOnHand` on parts is denormalized — always compute from `SUM(quantityDelta)`. Reason=`sale` for POS deductions. |
| **Sequence Number** | Human-readable document numbers (`SA-0001`, `INV-0001`) generated via a dedicated `sequences` table with atomic increment. One sequence per document type. |
| **Voided Sale** | A sale marked `status='voided'`. No stock reversal, no payment unallocation. Used to fix cashier errors. Manager-only (authorization deferred). |
| **Address Lookup** | External Belgian address data (BOSA BEVLG) synced into local tables for autocomplete. Currently only Flanders (`BE-VLG`) is loaded; Brussels and Wallonia are configured but not yet synced. Two tables: `postal_codes` (code → display name) and `address_streets` (unique street + municipality + postal code combos). Sync replaces all data per region within a transaction. |
| **Staff Member** | Shop employee — mechanic or manager. Stored in `users` table. Has `name`, `role` (`mechanic`/`manager`), `hourlyRate` (cents/hour), and `isActive` flag. Referenced by `repairs.assignedTo` and `workLogs.userId`. Not an authentication concept; purely operational. May be selected as the runtime [Active User](#active-user) via the header dropdown. |
| **Active User** | The currently active staff member for the browser session. Picked from the staff list via the header avatar dropdown. Persisted in `localStorage` under `veloflow.activeStaffId`. **No real authentication** — purely a runtime pointer for future slice attribution (e.g., "sale created by...", "repair assigned to..."). When the active staff record is missing or `isActive=false` on refetch, the session clears automatically. |
